The baseline Random Forest achieved 0.6948 with a high train/CV gap (0.1789), indicating overfitting or insufficient regularization. The Logistic Regression candidate (iter01_c1) showed the best CV score (0.7014) with a very low gap, suggesting linear separability and benefit from L2 regularization. Extra Trees (0.721) had a lower gap but slightly worse performance than LR on this specific dataset profile, possibly due to high variance in tree depth settings. Gradient Boosting (0.7109) performed well but used standard preprocessing. To improve upon the best single model (LR) and address potential non-linear interactions missed by linear models, we propose a Voting ensemble combining LR (strong regularization) with Extra Trees (high capacity). We also propose a Pipeline approach to explicitly test if feature scaling improves the Random Forest's stability compared to the median imputation baseline. All candidates use balanced class weights to mitigate the slight imbalance.
